# Growing deletion moduli: exact tail admission boundary

- **Stage:** 3-formalized / not_new_scientific_knowledge
- **Type:** THEOREM (Lean), auxiliary classification; proposed RH mechanism rejected at its first gate
- **RH status:** no new zero-forced relation or RH implication.

## Question and intended chain

The proposed chain was literal zeta coefficients → simultaneous arithmetic histories at a zero
→ a new cross-modulus compatibility relation → exclusion of off-line zeros. The corpus already
constructs all finite word lengths in one norm limit for each fixed modulus when Re(s)>1/2.
The test here asks whether making the modulus range grow supplies the missing relation.

Write a_q(n)=1-(q+1)[q+1 divides n], so q denotes one less than the actual modulus, and
P_q(s,N)=sum_(1<=n<=N) a_q(n)n^(-s). The existing exact coefficient prefix is N mod (q+1).
Its Abel tail bound is proportional to q(N+1)^(-Re(s)). No zero assumption enters that bound.

## Closed statement and proof

For sigma=Re(s)>0, N>=1 and 1<=A<=N, define the tail oscillation as
sup_(q<=A, K,M>=N) |P_q(s,K)-P_q(s,M)|. It has the two bounds

    A [2(N+1)]^(-sigma)
       <= tail oscillation
       <= 2 A (1+|s|/sigma) (N+1)^(-sigma).

The upper bound applies the existing finite Abel block estimate at min(K,M), whose negative
power is at most (N+1)^(-sigma). No passage to an infinite limit is needed for either bound. For the lower bound choose q=A and the first positive multiple
k of A+1 strictly after N. Then N<k<=N+A+1<=2(N+1). The difference between prefixes k and
k-1 is exactly -A k^(-s), of norm A k^(-sigma).

Consequently, for any integer-valued budget A(N)<=N, uniform tail convergence over q<=A(N)
is equivalent to A(N)(N+1)^(-sigma) tending to zero. This is an ordinary cutoff resource
law, independent of whether zeta(s) vanishes. For sigma<=1, the maximal budget A(N)=N
already fails to converge uniformly; allowing every modulus fails as well.

The critical-strip statement is stronger: for every 0<sigma<=1 and every natural-valued A,
without a growth or monotonicity assumption,

    uniform tails over q<=A(N)  iff  A(N)(N+1)^(-sigma) -> 0.

To remove the budget restriction, uniform tails first force A(N)<N eventually. Otherwise the
sub-budget q<=N has tail oscillation at least 2^(-sigma)/2, since
N(N+1)^(-sigma)>=N/(N+1)>=1/2 for N>=1. Apply the bounded-budget criterion to min(A(N),N),
which then equals A(N) eventually. The reverse direction uses the same upper bound directly.
The bounded-budget theorem holds for all sigma>0; the unrestricted-budget theorem stated here
is limited to 0<sigma<=1. No result for arbitrary budgets at sigma>1 is asserted in this leaf.

- **Killing mechanism:** a single deletion event prevents modulus-uniform scalar convergence
  throughout 0<Re(s)<=1. A zero cannot remove that event from the literal prefix sequence.
- **Positive survivor:** the exact growing-budget criterion above, including arbitrary budgets in
  the critical strip. It quantifies precisely which restricted uniformity survives.
- **Interpretation:** within the stated domain this convergence demand depends only on Re(s) and
  the budget, so points with the same real part have the same admission criterion. It does not rule out a separate relation between completed histories.
- **Status:** dependency-closed paper proof and ten closed Lean theorems in
  `formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/EulerDeletionGrowingModulus.lean`, namespace
  `RHTower.DeletionModulusBoundary`. The exact capstone is
  `uniformTails_iff_budget_decay_critical`; the negative corollary is `not_all_moduli_uniform`.
  This positive classification closes the no-go audit; it is not being presented as new
  scientific knowledge or as a qualifying RH architecture.

# Equicontinuity in metric spaces

This file contains various facts about (uniform) equicontinuity in metric spaces. Most
importantly, we prove the usual characterization of equicontinuity of `F` at `x₀` in the case of
(pseudo) metric spaces: `∀ ε > 0, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ x, dist x x₀ < δ → ∀ i, dist (F i x₀) (F i x) < ε`,
and we prove that functions sharing a common (local or global) continuity modulus are
(locally or uniformly) equicontinuous.

* `Metric.equicontinuousAt_iff`: characterization of equicontinuity for families of functions
  between (pseudo) metric spaces.
* `Metric.equicontinuousAt_of_continuity_modulus`: convenient way to prove equicontinuity at a
  point of a family of functions to a (pseudo) metric space by showing that they share a common
  *local* continuity modulus.
* `Metric.uniformEquicontinuous_of_continuity_modulus`: convenient way to prove uniform
  equicontinuity of a family of functions to a (pseudo) metric space by showing that they share a
  common *global* continuity modulus.

## Tags

equicontinuity, continuity modulus

# Chen--Gupta--Li Lemma 6.2: primitive Dirichlet root-number norm

Mathlib defines the root number by a normalized Gauss sum but does not expose
the norm-one theorem needed to make CGL's far-left functional estimate uniform
in the primitive character.  This module proves that fact from the primitive
Fourier-transform formula and exact finite cyclic Parseval.
-/

open Complex LSeries

/-- **Primitive Dirichlet root numbers have norm one.**  This closes the
root-number factor in CGL's functional-equation bound without placing any
extra premise in the public theorem. -/
theorem cglLemma62_primitive_rootNumber_norm_one
    (P : CGLLemma62PrimitiveCharacter) : ‖P.character.rootNumber‖ = 1 := by
  classical
  letI : NeZero P.modulus.value := ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt P.modulus.positive⟩
  let g : ℂ := gaussSum P.character ZMod.stdAddChar
  let C : ℝ := ∑ a : ZMod P.modulus.value, Complex.normSq (P.character a)
  have hCpos : 0 < C := by
    have hone : Complex.normSq (P.character (1 : ZMod P.modulus.value)) = 1 := by
      simp [Complex.normSq_eq_norm_sq]
    have hle : Complex.normSq (P.character (1 : ZMod P.modulus.value)) ≤ C := by
      exact Finset.single_le_sum
        (fun a _ => Complex.normSq_nonneg (P.character a)) (Finset.mem_univ _)
    linarith
  have hinvNorm (a : ZMod P.modulus.value) :
      Complex.normSq (P.character⁻¹ a) = Complex.normSq (P.character a) := by
    by_cases ha : IsUnit a
    · rw [← ha.unit_spec]
      simp only [Complex.normSq_eq_norm_sq]
      rw [DirichletCharacter.unit_norm_eq_one,
        DirichletCharacter.unit_norm_eq_one]
    · rw [MulChar.map_nonunit _ ha, MulChar.map_nonunit _ ha]
  have hinvSum :
      ∑ k : ZMod P.modulus.value, Complex.normSq (P.character⁻¹ (-k)) = C := by
    calc
      _ = ∑ k : ZMod P.modulus.value, Complex.normSq (P.character⁻¹ k) := by
        exact Finset.sum_equiv (Equiv.neg (ZMod P.modulus.value)) (by simp)
          (fun _ _ => rfl)
      _ = C := by
        simp only [C]
        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun k _ => hinvNorm k)
  have hnormSq : Complex.normSq g = (P.modulus.value : ℝ) := by
    have hparse := GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.fieldOneFiniteCyclicFourier_parseval
      P.modulus.value P.character
    simp_rw [P.primitive.fourierTransform_eq_inv_mul_gaussSum,
      Complex.normSq_mul] at hparse
    rw [← Finset.sum_mul, hinvSum] at hparse
    change C * Complex.normSq g = (P.modulus.value : ℝ) * C at hparse
    apply mul_left_cancel₀ hCpos.ne'
    calc
      C * Complex.normSq g = (P.modulus.value : ℝ) * C := hparse
      _ = C * (P.modulus.value : ℝ) := mul_comm _ _
  have hnorm : ‖g‖ = (P.modulus.value : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) := by
    calc
      ‖g‖ = √(Complex.normSq g) := Complex.norm_def g
      _ = √(P.modulus.value : ℝ) := by rw [hnormSq]
      _ = (P.modulus.value : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) := Real.sqrt_eq_rpow _
  change ‖g / I ^ (if P.character.Even then 0 else 1) /
    (P.modulus.value : ℂ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℂ)‖ = 1
  have hqpos : 0 < (P.modulus.value : ℝ) := by
    exact_mod_cast P.modulus.positive
  rw [norm_div, norm_div, norm_pow, Complex.norm_I, one_pow,
    Complex.norm_natCast_cpow_of_pos P.modulus.positive, hnorm]
  simpa using (div_self (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hqpos (1 / 2 : ℝ)).ne')

end

      nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameResidueStdAddChar K y ↔
      x - y ∈ (nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameMilnorResidue K).ker := by
  constructor
  · intro hphase
    change nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameMilnorResidue K (x - y) = 0
    rw [map_sub]
    apply sub_eq_zero.mpr
    apply finiteMilnorKOneStdAddChar_injective
    exact hphase
  · intro hkernel
    change finiteMilnorKOneStdAddChar _ (nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameMilnorResidue K x) =
      finiteMilnorKOneStdAddChar _ (nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameMilnorResidue K y)
    have hresidue : nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameMilnorResidue K x =
        nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameMilnorResidue K y := by
      apply sub_eq_zero.mp
      rw [← (nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameMilnorResidue K).map_sub]
      exact hkernel
    exact congrArg (finiteMilnorKOneStdAddChar _) hresidue

/-- At a finite number-field place, the residue-normalized phase is one exactly at zero tame
residue. -/
theorem numberFieldFinitePlace_tameResidueStdAddChar_eq_one_iff_mem_tameKernel
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [NumberField K] (v : NumberField.FinitePlace K)
    (x : MilnorKDeg (completion K (.finite v)) 2) :
    nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameResidueStdAddChar (completion K (.finite v)) x = 1 ↔

  nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameResidueStdAddChar_eq_one_iff_mem_tameKernel
    (completion K (.finite v)) x

/-- At a finite place of `F(t)`, the residue-normalized phase is one exactly at zero tame
residue. -/
theorem rationalFunctionFinitePlace_tameResidueStdAddChar_eq_one_iff_mem_tameKernel
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F] (v : HeightOneSpectrum F[X])
    (x : MilnorKDeg (rationalFunctionCompletion F (.finite v)) 2) :
    nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameResidueStdAddChar
      (rationalFunctionCompletion F (.finite v)) x = 1 ↔
      x ∈ (nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameMilnorResidue
        (rationalFunctionCompletion F (.finite v))).ker :=
  nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameResidueStdAddChar_eq_one_iff_mem_tameKernel
    (rationalFunctionCompletion F (.finite v)) x

/-- At the infinite place of `F(t)`, the residue-normalized phase is one exactly at zero tame
residue. -/
theorem rationalFunctionInfinitePlace_tameResidueStdAddChar_eq_one_iff_mem_tameKernel
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F]
    (x : MilnorKDeg (rationalFunctionCompletion F .infinite) 2) :
    nonarchimedeanLocalFieldTameResidueStdAddChar
      (rationalFunctionCompletion F .infinite) x = 1 ↔

:= by
  ext i
  simp [deningerTopConormalResidue, deningerTopConormalEmbedding]

/-- **Trace equals different times residue.** Top residue after the ramified different is rank
times coordinate-zero extraction. -/
theorem deningerTopConormalResidue_differentAction
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (n : ℕ)
    (y : DeningerRamifiedBlockHilbert (ι × Fin (n + 1))) :
    deningerTopConormalResidue n (deningerRamifiedDifferentAction n y) =
      ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ) • deningerRawPowerResidue n y := by
  rw [deningerRamifiedDifferentAction, deningerTopConormalResidue_embedding]

/-- Final-coordinate embedding is an isometry for the standard finite Hilbert metrics. -/
theorem inner_deningerTopConormalEmbedding
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (n : ℕ)
    (x y : DeningerRamifiedBlockHilbert ι) :
    inner ℂ (deningerTopConormalEmbedding n x) (deningerTopConormalEmbedding n y) =
      inner ℂ x y := by
  rw [inner_deningerTopConormalEmbedding_left,
    deningerTopConormalResidue_embedding]

/-- Final-residue extraction commutes with scalar multiplication. -/
theorem deningerTopConormalResidue_smul
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (n : ℕ) (c : ℂ)
    (y : DeningerRamifiedBlockHilbert (ι × Fin (n + 1))) :
    deningerTopConormalResidue n (c • y) =
      c • deningerTopConormalResidue n y := by
  ext i
  simp [deningerTopConormalResidue]

/-- Rank-half-density normalized top-conormal power transfer, of degree `n+1`. -/
def deningerTopConormalTransfer {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (n : ℕ)
    (x : DeningerRamifiedBlockHilbert ι) :
    DeningerRamifiedBlockHilbert (ι × Fin (n + 1)) :=
  ((Real.sqrt (n + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) • deningerTopConormalEmbedding n x

/-- Rank-half-density normalized residue cotransfer, of degree `n+1`. -/
def deningerTopConormalCotransfer {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (n : ℕ)
    (y : DeningerRamifiedBlockHilbert (ι × Fin (n + 1))) :
    DeningerRamifiedBlockHilbert ι :=
  ((Real.sqrt (n + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) • deningerTopConormalResidue n y

/-- The normalized residue cotransfer is the Hilbert adjoint of normalized conormal transfer. -/
theorem deningerTopConormalTransfer_adjoint
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (n : ℕ)
    (x : DeningerRamifiedBlockHilbert ι)
    (y : DeningerRamifiedBlockHilbert (ι × Fin (n + 1))) :
    inner ℂ (deningerTopConormalTransfer n x) y =
      inner ℂ x (deningerTopConormalCotransfer n y) := by
  rw [deningerTopConormalTransfer, deningerTopConormalCotransfer,
    inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right, Complex.conj_ofReal,
    inner_deningerTopConormalEmbedding_left]

/-- **Ramified degree law.** Normalized residue after normalized conormal transfer is
`(n+1) • id`. -/
theorem deningerTopConormalCotransfer_transfer
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (n : ℕ)
    (x : DeningerRamifiedBlockHilbert ι) :
    deningerTopConormalCotransfer n (deningerTopConormalTransfer n x) =
      ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ) • x := by
  rw [deningerTopConormalCotransfer, deningerTopConormalTransfer,
    deningerTopConormalResidue_smul, deningerTopConormalResidue_embedding, smul_smul]
  congr 1
  norm_cast
  exact Real.mul_self_sqrt (Nat.cast_nonneg _)

/-!
# Boundary limits of the spectral-xi heat residues

The fixed-time heat coefficients were originally derived as genuine local
residues of `logDeriv riemannXiSpectral`.  This file carries that complex
residue series itself to the real boundary.  Each normalized local residue
converges to its boundary heat residue, the complete boundary residue series
is summable, and the entire normalized interior residue sum converges to it.

This makes the connection to the spectral-xi logarithmic derivative explicit
at the complete-series level rather than only after forgetting to real-valued
heat sums.
-/

open Complex Filter MeasureTheory Metric Polynomial Set Topology
open scoped Classical ENNReal Interval Topology

namespace RiemannGaussian

noncomputable section

/-- The complex fixed-time boundary residue contributed by one spectral
zero. -/
def riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidue
    (x tau : ℝ) (rho : NontrivialZetaZero) : ℂ :=
  (zetaUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatSummand x tau rho : ℂ)

/-- A genuine interior heat-weighted spectral-xi residue, divided by `2*y`,
converges to its complex boundary heat residue. -/
theorem tendsto_riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatResidue_boundaryQuotient
    (x : ℝ) {tau : ℝ} (htau : 0 < tau)
    (rho : NontrivialZetaZero) :
    Tendsto
      (fun y : ℝ ↦
        riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatResidue
            (upperBoundaryApproachPoint x y) tau rho /
          ((2 * y : ℝ) : ℂ))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0))
      (nhds (riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidue x tau rho)) := by
  have hreal :=
    tendsto_zetaUpperHyperbolicHeatSummand_boundaryQuotient x htau rho
  have hcomplex : Tendsto
      (fun y : ℝ ↦ ((zetaUpperHyperbolicHeatSummand
        (upperBoundaryApproachPoint x y) tau rho / (2 * y) : ℝ) : ℂ))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0))
      (nhds ((zetaUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatSummand x tau rho : ℝ) : ℂ)) :=
    tendsto_ofReal_iff.mpr hreal
  apply hcomplex.congr'
  filter_upwards with y
  rw [riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatResidue_eq_ofReal]
  push_cast
  rfl

/-- The complete complex boundary residue series sums to the embedded real
boundary heat total. -/
theorem hasSum_riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidue
    (x : ℝ) {tau : ℝ} (htau : 0 < tau) :
    HasSum (riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidue x tau)
      (riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatTotal x tau : ℂ) := by
  exact Complex.hasSum_ofReal.mpr
    (summable_zetaUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatSummand x htau).hasSum

/-- The complete complex fixed-time boundary heat-residue sum. -/
def riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidueTotal
    (x tau : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  ∑' rho : NontrivialZetaZero,
    riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidue x tau rho

/-- The complex boundary residue total is exactly the embedded positive real
boundary heat total. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidueTotal_eq_ofReal
    (x : ℝ) {tau : ℝ} (htau : 0 < tau) :
    riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidueTotal x tau =
      (riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatTotal x tau : ℂ) := by
  exact
    (hasSum_riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidue x htau).tsum_eq

/-- Vanishing of the complete complex boundary residue total is exactly
RH. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidueTotal_eq_zero_iff_rh
    (x : ℝ) {tau : ℝ} (htau : 0 < tau) :
    riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidueTotal x tau = 0 ↔
      RiemannHypothesis := by
  rw [riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatResidueTotal_eq_ofReal
    x htau, Complex.ofReal_eq_zero]
  exact riemannXiUpperHyperbolicBoundaryHeatTotal_eq_zero_iff_rh x htau

/-- The complete interior heat-weighted residue series divided termwise by
the exact boundary factor. -/
def riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatResidueBoundaryQuotient
    (x tau y : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  ∑' rho : NontrivialZetaZero,
    riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatResidue
        (upperBoundaryApproachPoint x y) tau rho /
      ((2 * y : ℝ) : ℂ)

/-- At positive height the normalized complex residue series is the embedded
normalized real spectral heat sum. -/
theorem riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatResidueBoundaryQuotient_eq
    (x : ℝ) {tau y : ℝ} (htau : 0 < tau) (hy : 0 < y) :
    riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatResidueBoundaryQuotient x tau y =
      (riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatSum
          (upperBoundaryApproachPoint x y) tau : ℂ) /
        ((2 * y : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
  unfold riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatResidueBoundaryQuotient
  exact ((hasSum_riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatResidue
    (by simpa using hy) htau).div_const ((2 * y : ℝ) : ℂ)).tsum_eq

/-- The entire normalized complex spectral-xi residue series converges to the
complete boundary heat residue total. -/
theorem tendsto_riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatResidueBoundaryQuotient
    (x : ℝ) {tau : ℝ} (htau : 0 < tau) :
    Tendsto
      (riemannXiUpperHyperbolicHeatResidueBoundaryQuotient x tau)
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0))

/-!
# Norm-normalized tame phases at completed finite places of `F(t)`

Global projective-line reciprocity does not use an independently chosen character of every finite
residue field.  Its local term is the base-field character after the Bass--Tate norm.  This module
transports exactly that norm-normalized residue character through completion and composes it with
the concrete adic tame residue.

The resulting local phase is therefore normalized exactly as the finite terms in the proven global
Milnor reciprocity law.  This is a tame Milnor analogue of the normalization compatibility required
by Albert--Brauer--Hasse--Noether.  It does not identify Milnor `K₂` with a Brauer group.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ABHN

open IsDedekindDomain
open scoped Polynomial WithZero WithZeroMulInt

universe u

noncomputable section

/-- The global norm-normalized residue character transported to the completed residue field. -/
noncomputable def rationalFunctionFiniteAdicNormResidueStdAddChar
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F] (q : MonicIrred F) :
    AddChar (MilnorKDeg (IsLocalRing.ResidueField
      ((Valued.v : Valuation
        ((polyPlace q.2.1).adicCompletion (RatFunc F)) ℤᵐ⁰).valuationSubring)) 1) ℂ :=
  (finiteMilnorKOneStdAddChar F).compAddMonoidHom
    ((milnorNormAt q 1).comp
      (rationalFunctionAdicCompletion_valuationResidueMilnorKDegAddEquiv
        F (polyPlace q.2.1) 1).symm.toAddMonoidHom)

/-- Transporting a global-place residue and then evaluating the completed residue character gives
exactly the finite norm phase occurring in global reciprocity. -/
theorem rationalFunctionFiniteAdicNormResidueStdAddChar_apply_equiv
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F] (q : MonicIrred F)
    (x : MilnorKDeg (polyResidueField q.2.1) 1) :
    rationalFunctionFiniteAdicNormResidueStdAddChar F q
        (rationalFunctionAdicCompletion_valuationResidueMilnorKDegAddEquiv
          F (polyPlace q.2.1) 1 x) =
      finiteMilnorKOneStdAddChar F (milnorNormAt q 1 x) := by
  change finiteMilnorKOneStdAddChar F
    (milnorNormAt q 1
      ((rationalFunctionAdicCompletion_valuationResidueMilnorKDegAddEquiv
        F (polyPlace q.2.1) 1).symm
          (rationalFunctionAdicCompletion_valuationResidueMilnorKDegAddEquiv
            F (polyPlace q.2.1) 1 x))) = _
  rw [AddEquiv.symm_apply_apply]

/-- Norm of the transported concrete adic tame residue.  This is the completed local additive
invariant whose circle character is globally normalized. -/
noncomputable def rationalFunctionFiniteAdicNormTameMilnorInvariant
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F] (q : MonicIrred F) :
    MilnorKDeg ((polyPlace q.2.1).adicCompletion (RatFunc F)) 2 →+
      MilnorKDeg F 1 :=
  (milnorNormAt q 1).comp
    ((rationalFunctionAdicCompletion_valuationResidueMilnorKDegAddEquiv
      F (polyPlace q.2.1) 1).symm.toAddMonoidHom.comp
        (rationalFunctionFiniteAdicTameMilnorResidue F (polyPlace q.2.1)))

/-- The norm-normalized completed tame phase at `q`. -/
noncomputable def rationalFunctionFiniteAdicNormTameStdAddChar
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F] (q : MonicIrred F) :
    AddChar (MilnorKDeg ((polyPlace q.2.1).adicCompletion (RatFunc F)) 2) ℂ :=
  (finiteMilnorKOneStdAddChar F).compAddMonoidHom
    (rationalFunctionFiniteAdicNormTameMilnorInvariant F q)

/-- Evaluation formula for the norm-normalized completed tame phase. -/
theorem rationalFunctionFiniteAdicNormTameStdAddChar_apply
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F] (q : MonicIrred F)
    (x : MilnorKDeg ((polyPlace q.2.1).adicCompletion (RatFunc F)) 2) :
    rationalFunctionFiniteAdicNormTameStdAddChar F q x =
      finiteMilnorKOneStdAddChar F
        (milnorNormAt q 1
          ((rationalFunctionAdicCompletion_valuationResidueMilnorKDegAddEquiv
            F (polyPlace q.2.1) 1).symm
              (rationalFunctionFiniteAdicTameMilnorResidue F (polyPlace q.2.1) x))) :=
  rfl

/-- Phase one means exactly that the norm of the transported tame residue vanishes. -/
theorem rationalFunctionFiniteAdicNormTameStdAddChar_eq_one_iff_norm_tameResidue_eq_zero
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Finite F] (q : MonicIrred F)
    (x : MilnorKDeg ((polyPlace q.2.1).adicCompletion (RatFunc F)) 2) :
    rationalFunctionFiniteAdicNormTameStdAddChar F q x = 1 ↔
      milnorNormAt q 1
        ((rationalFunctionAdicCompletion_valuationResidueMilnorKDegAddEquiv
          F (polyPlace q.2.1) 1).symm
            (rationalFunctionFiniteAdicTameMilnorResidue F (polyPlace q.2.1) x)) = 0 := by
  rw [rationalFunctionFiniteAdicNormTameStdAddChar_apply]
  exact finiteMilnorKOneStdAddChar_eq_one_iff_eq_zero F _
